finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q query parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL string via an f-string, so an attacker can alter the query (e.g. UNION SELECT to read other tables/columns such as price or owner or any table in shop.db).
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') takes raw user input with no validation
term is embedded in the SQL text via f-string, not bound as a parameter
query results are returned to the caller as JSON, so injected UNION output is exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping, or parameter binding on this path; no authentication or authorization decorators on the route. Contrast: /product (app.py:18) and /by-owner (app.py:25) use parameterized queries, so they are not vulnerable.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads q unvalidated and app.py:12 f-string-interpolates it into the SQL passed to db.execute, with no decorators, escaping or binding on the unauthenticated route, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so UNION-based exfiltration works (sqlite3 blocks stacked statements, but UNION SELECT is unaffected).
